S34.01.needs: a conversation with several messages that contain a shared word
S34.01.note: The Command+F listener is in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx; the on-screen control for opening it was not confirmed.
steps: Open a conversation that has several messages.
Press Command+F. A bar with the placeholder "Search messages..." appears.
Type a word that appears in the conversation.
Click "Go to next match" or "Go to previous match" (or press Enter and Shift+Enter in the box).
Check the match count beside the box and that the view jumps between the matching messages, as Expected says.
S34.01.where: Open a conversation with messages > press Command+F (or click the search control in the chat header if shown)

S34.02.needs: a Free or paid account with at least one past conversation containing a known word
S34.02.note: Which conversations are visible in history is decided by the server route apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts, not by visible text.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar, or press Shift+Command+F.
Type a word from a past conversation's title or messages in the box "Search your workspace" and press Enter.
Leave the category on "All" and read the results list.
Click a result that is a conversation and check that it opens that chat.
Compare with Expected: titles and message text are both matched and the chat opens.
S34.02.where: Sidebar > Search > Search your workspace (type a title or message text, press Enter)

S34.03.needs: a Free or paid account with at least one Project
S34.03.note: The Projects page search field was found in ProjectGallery.tsx; I did not confirm that the Projects page is the screen a person reaches from the sidebar label.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar.
Type the name or a word from the description of a project.
Click the category chip "Projects" under the box, then read the results.
Click a result with the project's name and check that it opens that project.
Compare with Expected: the project is found by name or description.
S34.03.where: Sidebar > Search > Projects (category chip), or Sidebar > Projects > Search projects...

S34.04.needs: a Free or paid account with some saved files, images or documents in Library
S34.04.note: The box's accessible name is "Search the library by name"; the API passes the query to the server, and I did not verify whether prompt text is also matched.
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Click in the box "Search files and projects" and type part of a file name.
Watch the list narrow to matching items.
Clear the box and check that the full list returns.
Compare with Expected: the box filters Library items by name.
S34.04.where: Sidebar > Library > Search files and projects

S34.05.needs: a Free or paid account with at least one saved artifact
S34.05.note: The old route /chat/artifacts redirects to the Library surface filter; content matching beyond the title was not confirmed.
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Click the tab "Artifacts" under the search box.
Type part of an artifact's title in "Search files and projects".
Click the matching artifact to open it.
Compare with Expected: the artifact is found by title and opens.
S34.05.where: Sidebar > Library > Artifacts (tab) > Search files and projects

S34.06.needs: a paid account with at least one connected work source (Drive, Slack or Notion)
S34.06.note: The submenu shows a coming-soon item when connectors are not released, and the server-side retrieval was not checked.
steps: Open a new chat and click the "+" in the composer.
Click "Connectors" to open its submenu.
Turn on a connected source (for example Drive or Slack) with its checkbox.
Send a question that asks for information stored in that source.
Compare with Expected: the answer draws on the connected source.

S34.07.note: The menu item was found in AttachmentMenu.tsx; I did not confirm it is the exact menu the web composer shows.
steps: Open a new chat and click the "+" in the composer.
Click "Search the web" to turn it on, then check the chip that shows "Web search".
Ask a question about a current public topic.
Read the answer and look for sources or citations from the web.
S34.07.where: Chat composer > + > Search the web (menu item; the active chip reads "Web search")

S34.15.needs: a Free or paid account with past conversations spread over several dates
S34.15.note: The Filters panel only appears when the search can filter conversations; filtered-result accuracy is not verified by the code read.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar and type a query.
Click the "Filters" button under the box.
Click "From Date" and pick a date, then "To Date" and pick a later date.
Read the results list and check that every result falls inside the chosen range.
Compare with Expected: results outside the range are not shown.
S34.15.where: Sidebar > Search > Filters > From Date / To Date

S34.19.note: Found the project Sources panel (apps/web/features/projects/components/SourcesPanel.tsx) with filter, sort and search controls, but found no visible control for a named source collection or for limiting chats to one.

S34.20.note: Only recent searches were found; no popular or typed-completion suggestions were found in the code.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar and run one search so it is stored.
Close the dialog, open "Search" again and leave the box empty.
Look for the "Recent Searches" heading with query chips under it.
Click a chip and check that the query runs.
Compare with Expected: a previous query is offered and can be picked.
S34.20.where: Sidebar > Search > Recent Searches (shown when the box is empty)

S34.21.needs: a Free or paid account; follow-up suggestions must be turned on in settings
S34.21.note: The suggestions show only when the follow-up setting is on, so the settings label was not checked.
steps: Send a question that uses web search and wait for the answer to finish.
Look below the answer for the region "Follow-up suggestions".
Click one suggestion.
Check that it is sent as the next message in the chat.
Compare with Expected: a tap sends the refined query.
S34.21.where: Chat > under the latest answer > Follow-up suggestions

S34.22.needs: a query that the assistant finds ambiguous
S34.22.note: Found the clarify tool name ask_clarifying_questions in apps/web/lib/services/clarify-tool-service.ts and a clarify card at apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/ClarifyCard.tsx, but did not read its visible wording or confirm the path a person takes.

S34.23.needs: a Free or paid account with a known word in past chats
S34.23.note: Result previews in the dialog were found; citation previews are covered under S34.25.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar and type a word you know is in a chat.
Press Enter and wait for the results.
Read each result: it shows a type label (for example "Title", "Project" or "Artifact") and the matched word in highlight.
Compare with Expected: each result shows a preview before it is opened.
S34.23.where: Sidebar > Search > type a query > results list

S34.24.needs: a Free or paid account with web search turned on
S34.24.note: Card fields (title, site, link) were not read line by line.
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Click the "Sources" button under the answer.
Read the sections "Citations" and "More" in the panel.
Check that each source card shows a title, site and link.
Compare with Expected: each source card has at least title, site and link.
S34.24.where: Chat > answer with web sources > "Sources" button under the answer > Citations / More

S34.25.needs: a Free or paid account with web search turned on
S34.25.note: The chip preview is built in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx; the exact preview words for title and snippet were not extracted.
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Hover (or tap on a touch screen) over a citation chip in the answer text.
Read the preview that opens over the answer.
Check it shows the source title, site and snippet.
Compare with Expected: the preview shows without leaving the answer.
S34.25.where: Chat > answer with citations > hover or tap a numbered citation chip

S34.26.needs: a Free or paid account with web search turned on, and an answer with several sources
S34.26.note: The count label is a translation template; the spoken number depends on how many sources the answer has.
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Click the compact line "View N sources" under the answer.
Look for the "More" section after "Citations".
Compare the full list with the sources the answer used and consulted.
Compare with Expected: the compact summary expands to the full list.
S34.26.where: Chat > answer > "View N sources" button > More

S34.27.needs: a Free or paid account with web search turned on
S34.27.note: The links open in a new tab (target _blank) in CitationChip.tsx and ResearchPanel.tsx; the visible link text was not extracted.
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Click a citation chip, or a source in the Sources panel.
Check that a new browser tab opens with the original page.
Compare with Expected: the original page or document opens.
S34.27.where: Chat > answer > click a citation chip or a source card title

S34.31.needs: a Free or paid account with web search turned on
S34.31.note: The date appears only when the source has the date data; the Sources panel date display was not confirmed.
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Hover or tap a citation chip.
Read the date line that starts with "Retrieved" and any published date above it.
Compare with Expected: the source shows its publication or retrieval date.
S34.31.where: Chat > answer > hover or tap a citation chip > read the "Retrieved" line

S34.32.note: The unavailable state shows "Search could not be completed" with a "Retry" button; reaching it needs the search service to fail, which a tester cannot trigger from the UI.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar.
Type a word that matches nothing and press Enter.
Read the empty state: "No results found" with "Try different keywords or clear filters".
Check that old results are not kept on screen.
Compare with Expected: an explicit empty state is shown.
S34.32.where: Sidebar > Search > type a nonsense word (for example zzqx9) and press Enter
